title: Quiz: Effect of Surface Area on Rate

questions.stem: How does breaking a solid reactant into smaller pieces affect the rate of reaction?

options.text: It has no effect on the rate
It increases the rate because the activation energy decreases
It increases the rate because the total surface area is larger
It decreases the rate because the pieces are lighter

questions.explanation: Smaller pieces have a larger total surface area exposed to the other reactant, meaning more particles on the surface can collide at the same time, increasing the rate.

questions.stem: Using collision theory, why does a powdered solid react faster than a large lump of the same mass?

options.text: More particles are exposed on the surface, allowing more collisions with the other reactant
The powder has a lower activation energy
The powder has a higher temperature
The powder has a different chemical composition

questions.explanation: In a powder, more particles are exposed on the surface compared to a single lump. This means more collisions can occur between the solid particles and the liquid or gas reactant at any given moment.

questions.stem: Which form of calcium carbonate would react fastest with hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Fine powder
A single large lump
All forms would react at the same rate
A few medium-sized chips

questions.explanation: Fine powder has the largest surface area to volume ratio, so more calcium carbonate particles are exposed to the acid at once, resulting in the fastest rate of reaction.

questions.stem: Why can flour dust be a serious explosion hazard in mills and bakeries?

options.text: Flour is a highly toxic substance
Fine flour particles have a very large surface area, allowing extremely rapid combustion
Flour produces poisonous gases when heated
Flour reacts with water to produce hydrogen gas

questions.explanation: Fine flour dust particles have an enormous surface area to volume ratio. If ignited, the reaction with oxygen can occur extremely rapidly across this large surface area, causing an explosion.

questions.stem: In an experiment comparing lumps vs powder of the same reactant, what would be the same at the end of both reactions?

options.text: The time taken for the reaction to finish
The total amount of product formed
The gradient of the graph at the start
The rate of reaction throughout

questions.explanation: If the same mass of reactant is used, the total amount of product formed will be the same regardless of surface area. Surface area only affects how fast the product is formed, not the total amount.

questions.stem: Surface area affects rate only when one of the reactants is a:

options.text: Liquid
Gas
Dissolved substance
Solid

questions.explanation: Surface area is relevant when a solid reacts with a liquid or gas. Only particles on the surface of a solid can collide with other reactants, so changing the surface area affects the rate.

questions.stem: A student compares the rate of reaction between large marble chips and powdered marble with hydrochloric acid. Which is the correct control variable?

options.text: The size of the marble pieces
The time taken for the reaction
The mass of marble and concentration of acid used
The volume of gas collected

questions.explanation: To make it a fair test, the mass of marble and the concentration and volume of acid must be kept the same. Only the surface area (size of pieces) should be changed.
